svg.title: Who reads which plugin header of a WooCommerce extension
svg.desc: The header comment of the main plugin file has three groups of fields. Identity fields such as Plugin Name, Version, Author, Text Domain and Domain Path are shown on the WordPress Plugins screen. The requirement fields Requires at least, Requires PHP and Requires Plugins are checked by WordPress when the plugin is activated and the activation is refused with a message when one is not met. The WooCommerce fields WC requires at least, WC tested up to and Woo are added to the plugin data by WooCommerce; WC tested up to drives the untested extension warnings when WooCommerce is updated and the compatibility warnings, while Tested up to belongs only in readme.txt for WordPress.org.
svg.text: The plugin header and its readers
What WordPress 7.1.3 and WooCommerce 11.2.1 do with each field, as observed on the test site

g.text: Lists the plugin and links Plugin URI and
Author URI. Domain Path tells where the
translation files are. Not read: Tested up to,
Refuses to activate when WordPress or PHP is
too old, or a required plugin is missing or
inactive; WP-CLI printed the reason for each.
Slugs are WordPress.org slugs, for example
Adds the three headers to the plugin data.
WC tested up to feeds the untested-extensions
warning of major updates and the status report.
WC requires at least is stored, not enforced.

svg.text: L-1 policy: Requires at least and WC requires at least name the previous series, Tested up to (readme.txt) and WC tested up to name the current one.
For WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.2 that means 7.0 and 11.1 as minimums and 7.1 and 11.2 as tested versions.
